about.label: About
about.title: Why NAJDA exists
about.description: NAJDA simulates an emergency dispatch network end to end — not a real emergency service, and not connected to one.
about.sectionTitle: The problem we set out to model
about.sectionDescription: Real dispatch systems coordinate many independent actors — citizens, dispatchers, ambulance crews, police, firefighters, and hospitals — all working off the same incident, but each needing a different slice of it. We wanted to build that coordination for real, not fake it with a single flat dashboard.
about.sectionDescription2: Every workflow in NAJDA runs against a real backend: shift management ties a vehicle's availability to whether a crew is actually on duty for it, AI-assisted priority scoring is advisory only, and every status change is written to a persistent incident record. What isn't real is the emergency itself — nothing here dispatches an actual ambulance.

hero.description1: NAJDA models how a citizen's report becomes a coordinated emergency response—from dispatcher to ambulance, police, fire department, and hospital—all sharing one incident timeline.
hero.description2: Built as an academic simulation, the platform demonstrates workflows, communication, AI-assisted triage, and real-time synchronization found in modern emergency response systems while keeping human dispatchers in complete control of operational decisions.

workflow.description: Every emergency follows the same traceable lifecycle, ensuring every participant sees the correct information at the correct moment.
workflow.step1Body: A citizen submits an incident from the mobile app — location, description, and photo or video evidence.
workflow.step2Body: The AI service scores priority and flags likely duplicates. Nothing here is final until a dispatcher confirms it.
workflow.step3Body: A vehicle is assigned only once a crew is actively on shift for it. Responders get the mission the moment it's confirmed.
workflow.step4Body: Hospitals get advance notice when transport is inbound. Every state change is written to the incident's event history.

features.title: Built for real-time coordination.
features.description: Every component exists to demonstrate how modern emergency systems exchange information reliably, while keeping human operators in complete control.
features.feature1Body: Backend services coordinate over a live event layer, so a slow hospital lookup never blocks a dispatcher assigning a unit.
features.feature2Body: WebSocket push keeps every open dashboard and app in sync with vehicle position — no dashboard is ever polling for what already happened.
features.feature3Body: Priority scoring, duplicate detection, and hospital ranking are all advisory. No incident is ever auto-dispatched.
features.feature4Body: Every actor works off the same incident record, but only ever sees the slice of it their role is permitted to.
